reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disorder caused by variants in the PC gene, encoding the biotin-dependent mitochondrial enzyme pyruvate carboxylase
The enzyme converts pyruvate to oxaloacetate, an anaplerotic step essential for gluconeogenesis, the citric acid cycle and neurotransmitter synthesis
Presents with lactic acidosis, often accompanied by hypoglycaemia, and a raised lactate-to-pyruvate ratio
The severe neonatal (type B, often French) form causes overwhelming lactic acidosis, hyperammonaemia, citrullinaemia and early death
The milder infantile (type A, North American) form causes developmental delay, seizures and recurrent metabolic acidosis with lactic acidaemia
A characteristic biochemical pattern includes raised lactate, ketones, ammonia, citrulline and lysine with low aspartate
Anaplerotic therapy and avoidance of fasting form the mainstay of supportive management, but outcomes are generally poor
Because pyruvate carboxylase is biotin-dependent, it should be distinguished from biotinidase and holocarboxylase synthetase deficiencies
reference.pathophysiology: Pyruvate carboxylase catalyses the ATP-dependent, biotin-requiring carboxylation of pyruvate to oxaloacetate within mitochondria. This reaction replenishes citric acid cycle intermediates (anaplerosis) and provides oxaloacetate for gluconeogenesis and, in the brain, for aspartate and glutamate synthesis. Enzyme deficiency blocks gluconeogenesis, causing fasting hypoglycaemia, and diverts pyruvate towards lactate, producing lactic acidosis with an elevated lactate-to-pyruvate ratio. Depletion of oxaloacetate impairs the malate-aspartate shuttle and urea cycle function, contributing to hyperammonaemia and abnormal amino acids, while cerebral aspartate deficiency disturbs myelination and neurotransmitter metabolism.
additionalDifferentials: Multiple carboxylase deficiency (biotinidase or holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency)
Organic acidaemias with secondary lactic acidosis
Fatty acid oxidation defects presenting with hypoglycaemia
additionalInvestigations: Blood lactate, pyruvate and calculated lactate-to-pyruvate ratio
Plasma amino acids showing raised citrulline, lysine and proline with low aspartate
Plasma ammonia and blood glucose during metabolic decompensation
Enzyme activity assay in cultured fibroblasts
Molecular genetic testing of the PC gene
Neuroimaging assessing white matter and structural changes
redFlags: Severe neonatal lactic acidosis with hyperammonaemia and encephalopathy
Rapid neurological deterioration during intercurrent illness
Failure of acidosis to respond to conventional resuscitation
reference.prognosis: The severe neonatal form carries a very poor prognosis with early death, and even the milder infantile form is usually associated with significant developmental delay and recurrent metabolic crises. Rare attenuated cases with more residual enzyme activity have better outcomes.
pitfalls: Confusing it with pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, which typically shows a normal lactate-to-pyruvate ratio
Missing the diagnosis when lactic acidosis is attributed to sepsis or tissue hypoperfusion
Overlooking hyperammonaemia and the urea cycle contribution
Failing to prevent catabolism and fasting, which precipitate crises
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: There is no cure; provide anaplerotic dietary support with a high-carbohydrate intake and avoidance of prolonged fasting through frequent feeds or continuous overnight feeding
Consider citrate, aspartate or triheptanoin supplementation to replenish citric acid cycle intermediates under metabolic specialist supervision

Manage acute decompensation with intravenous glucose to reverse hypoglycaemia and support anaplerosis, correction of severe acidosis, and treatment of hyperammonaemia with nitrogen-scavenging agents such as sodium benzoate and, if needed, haemofiltration or dialysis
Trial biotin, the enzyme cofactor, although a response is not usually seen
Monitor lactate, ammonia, glucose, plasma amino acids and neurodevelopment
Coordinate care through a specialist metabolic team with dietetic input
Offer genetic counselling and family screening for this autosomal recessive PC gene disorder
